A.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: ORIGINAL opaque portrait 1024x1536 background strip for a top-down vertical-scrolling aircraft game, chapter TWO "Lost City". The image supplied is ONLY a reference for the hand-painted semi-realistic finish, muted blue-gray asphalt, gray concrete, restrained olive vegetation, overhead camera and soft upper-left daylight. DO NOT COPY its straight paired building rows, repetitive sidewalks, centerline or uniform street composition.
Primary request: reconstruct this as a believable ruined MODERN city district with convincing everyday buildings and an irregular damaged street. High overhead orthographic view; no horizon, no perspective vanishing point. Architecture must read as contemporary reinforced-concrete/steel apartment, office, retail or utility buildings: ordinary rectangular windows, horizontal floor slabs, flat roofs, rooftop AC equipment, simple parapets and structurally aligned columns. NO arches of any kind, vaulted windows, cathedral/temple/palace shapes, classical station entrances, Roman/Gothic masonry, grand curved ramps, ceremonial staircases, or buildings shaped like a fortress wall.
Composition: asymmetrical, varied building footprints/heights/setbacks, small gaps and side alleys, locally collapsed facades exposing credible floors. The two sides must NOT mirror each other or repeat identical blocks. Street width and curbs vary within the tile: broken sections of sidewalk, displaced curb stones, diagonal road fissures, subsidence patches, shallow uneven broken asphalt, rubble accumulating in a few irregular side pockets, faded intermittent paint rather than a perfectly straight dashed center line. Some eroded road edge and parking-bay fragments are welcome. Avoid a neat avenue, perfectly parallel continuous curbs, a tiled grid, evenly spaced decorative debris, or a central road made into a clean symmetrical funnel.
Keep a continuous quiet low-contrast dark asphalt flight corridor within the middle 40% (x=30%..70%); surface should have subtle natural cracks/patches, not a blank slab. Large rubble and buildings remain outside it; no giant crater blocking the center. Road margins may shift/set back asymmetrically across the outer 30% on either side. Top and bottom 5% keep the road opening centered, roughly x=25%..75%, with simple quiet connections and no major landmark cut at the edge, so companion strips can blend in a narrow overlap. Interior arrangements should be notably irregular.
All roofs, buildings, foundations, ground, road edges and rubble must form one physically connected scene. Preserve the Lost City theme. No moving vehicles or added parked vehicles (those are separate scenery sprites), clouds/fog/shadows of clouds, actors, aircraft, enemies, bullets, pickups, glow circles, UI, readable text, logos, watermark, grid overlays, or transparent areas. One final full-frame painted texture, not a concept sheet.
Segment A: an abandoned residential/service neighborhood. Place an ordinary damaged L-shaped apartment building with flat rooftop utilities along part of the left edge; on the opposite side use two lower rectangular neighborhood retail/office shells with a staggered setback and an exposed broken service courtyard. Do not fill both edges with continuous tall towers. Rectangular window bays, clear horizontal floor bands, broken facade panels, a few rooftop AC boxes and small olive plants establish recognizable modern construction. A damaged side-lane mouth and a broad diagonal asphalt repair scar make the road feel naturally uneven. Restrained environmental storytelling without increasing central visual noise.
